Confirmed the recommendation: 'In cases where you need multiple columns in combination to uniquely identify each row, we recommend you pass these columns as a list (unique_key = [user_id, session_number]), rather than a string expression'.
• docs.getdbt.com/reference/resource-configs/unique_key — confirmed unique_key references the compiled column name in the final table; if SELECT does `id AS user_id`, then `unique_key='id'` would fail because `id` doesn't exist in the output, only `user_id`. Confirms the SELECT-OUTPUT rule.
• Trino error wording verified consistent with trino.io/docs/467: a reference to a non-existent column in a generated MERGE statement produces `Column 'id' cannot be resolved` (the standard Trino missing-column error form).
